sentences.chinese: 接下来就是——努力解决你自己造成的问题。

sentences.english: Being proactive and coming to your manager with suggestions is likely to help you regain trust.
sentences.chinese: 积极主动地向你的经理提出建议，很可能有助于你重新获得信任。

sentences.english: Psychologists tell us that we tend to have a negativity bias – we are more likely to remember negative things.
sentences.chinese: 心理学家告诉我们，我们往往有消极偏见——我们更容易记住消极的事情。

sentences.english: This is why executive coach Dina Denham Smith tells us we need to make our progress in fixing the issue clear and visible.
sentences.chinese: 这就是为什么高管教练迪娜·德纳姆·史密斯告诉我们，我们需要让自己在解决问题上的进展清晰可见。

sentences.english: It's also important to apologise.
sentences.chinese: 道歉也很重要。

sentences.english: Showing genuine remorse demonstrates that we can take ownership of our blunders.
sentences.chinese: 表现出真诚的悔恨表明我们可以为自己的错误负责。

sentences.english: As well as looking at how we make amends for our mix-ups to other people, we also need to be honest with ourselves.
sentences.chinese: 除了考虑如何弥补我们对他人的影响之外，我们也需要对自己诚实。

sentences.english: Removing emotion is important.
sentences.chinese: 消除情绪很重要。

sentences.english: Shame from making a mistake can cloud our judgement when deciding how to respond.
sentences.chinese: 因犯错而产生的羞耻感会在决定如何回应时影响我们的判断。

sentences.english: It can also affect our perception of the mistake's seriousness – it's easy to exaggerate how bad something really is.
sentences.chinese: 它还会影响我们对错误严重性的认知——人们很容易夸大事情的糟糕程度。

sentences.english: Everyone makes mistakes.
sentences.chinese: 每个人都会犯错。

sentences.english: What's really important is how we address them.
sentences.chinese: 真正重要的是我们如何应对错误。

sentences.english: It's important to be reflective.
sentences.chinese: 进行反思很重要。

sentences.english: Consider if there's an underlying cause for the mistake, and how to prevent future slip-ups.
sentences.chinese: 考虑错误是否有潜在的原因，以及如何防止将来出现失误。

sentences.english: It can also be useful to seek advice from someone who's had similar experiences in the past.
sentences.chinese: 向有过类似经历的人寻求建议也可能很有用。

sentences.english: Combined with our own reflections, this can be a powerful way to grow in our job and be more successful.
sentences.chinese: 加上我们自己的反思，这可以成为在工作中成长并取得更大成功的有效途径。

sentences.english: Academics Jasmine Virhia and Grace Lordan highlight research showing that workplaces which replace fear and blame around mistakes with opportunities for self-reflection are more psychologically safe.
sentences.chinese: 学者贾斯敏·维尔希亚和格蕾丝·洛丹提请人们注意一项研究，该研究表明用自我反思的机会取代对错误的恐惧和责备的工作场所，会令人在心理上感到更加安全。

sentences.english: This allows people to learn from their mistakes, grow their skills, improve processes and ultimately productivity.
sentences.chinese: 这使人们能够从错误中学习，提升技能，改进流程，最终提高生产力。

sentences.english: Handled in the right way, by both employees and employers, mistakes can become a powerful tool for improvement.
sentences.chinese: 如果员工和雇主都处理得当，错误可以成为进步的有效工具。

title: Why forgetting is good for you
titleChinese: 为什么遗忘对人有好处
paragraphs: Have you ever bumped into someone and their name just doesn't come to you? Or, you walk into a room and suddenly can't recall why you're there? Being forgetful can be really annoying, sometimes even embarrassing. But what if I told you that there are actually good reasons for our memories fading away?

In a BBC interview, neuroscientist Charan Ranganath uses a hoarding analogy. We don't tend to store everything we've ever owned in our house. Similarly, we don't need to store all our memories either. He says, "If we didn't forget anything, we'd be hoarding memories, and you'd never be able to find what you want, when you want it." For example, you don't need to remember the hotel number weeks after you've left the hotel or memorise all the faces you pass on the street.

We also need to be able to forget things in order to update our memories with new information. Imagine you get used to the same school timetable or work schedule for a whole year, but the next year, you have new procedures or routines. Your brain needs to be flexible and forget irrelevant details in order to handle the new information. Or, maybe it's been 10 years since you last saw a distant relative. It's likely their face has changed a lot since then, so that memory needs to be updated as well.

And, if you've ever been convinced that you know a word, but it just doesn't pop into your head, you're not alone. This tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon may suggest that some things are not fully forgotten, just currently inaccessible. Those with a higher level of knowledge are more affected by this, according to studies such as 'Impact of knowledge and age on tip-of-the-tongue rates', because their brains have to sort through more information to find the word.

Memories are sometimes compared to a cliff: once they have crumbled, they are lost and cannot be retrieved. However, in their article 'Forgetfulness: Why your mind going blank can be a benefit', Sanjay Sarma and Luke Yoquinto write that forgetting, it seems, is "less like a cliff slowly collapsing into the sea, and more like a house deep in the woods that becomes harder and harder to find".

title: Explore the world without leaving home
titleChinese: 足不出户也能探索世界
paragraphs: Have you ever dreamt of strolling along the streets of Venice, climbing the Eiffel Tower or flying above the Grand Canyon? It's much easier to take a virtual holiday now than ever before. Doesn't it sound adventurous – travelling to breathtaking destinations around the world while never leaving the comfort of your own home?

Digital maps let you roam almost any location on the planet, meaning you can explore the night markets in Bangkok, hover over mountainous regions like the Himalayas or zoom in on tiny islands and imagine you're sunbathing and smelling the sea. Of course, you won't experience the weather and culture in exactly the same way, but at least it's an option.

If you are a nature lover, it's possible to take an interactive virtual tour, with the option of virtual commentary, of a national park like Yellowstone in the USA. This area has a lot of volcanic activity, so you can watch geysers erupt, see sulphur lakes and virtually hike iconic trails. Their website is full of videos walking you to famous viewpoints like Dragon's Mouth Spring and the cascading waterfall at Upper Falls. And then there are oceanic adventures too. National Geographic offers virtual underwater experiences so you can dive with sharks and other marine life, see coral reefs come alive and explore sunken shipwrecks.

You can now tour many museums and landmarks virtually too, like The British Museum in London. You can explore more than 60 galleries where you'll see priceless artefacts from around the world, like the Rosetta Stone, and famous paintings and sculptures. The Taj Mahal is another place you can visit virtually and at a 360-degree angle, so you can scale heights that would be almost impossible if you were there in person.

They say 'the world is your oyster'. So next time you get the travel bug, try a virtual escape. A shoestring budget is no problem – you can still explore the world, and you don't even need a passport.

sentences.english: Have you ever dreamt of strolling along the streets of Venice, climbing the Eiffel Tower or flying above the Grand Canyon?
sentences.chinese: 你是否曾梦想过漫步在威尼斯的街道上，攀登埃菲尔铁塔，或者飞越大峡谷上空？

sentences.english: It's much easier to take a virtual holiday now than ever before.
sentences.chinese: 如今，享受虚拟假期比以往任何时候都要容易得多。

sentences.english: Doesn't it sound adventurous – travelling to breathtaking destinations around the world while never leaving the comfort of your own home?
sentences.chinese: 这听起来不新奇刺激吗——足不出户，就能前往世界各地令人惊叹的目的地旅行？

sentences.english: Digital maps let you roam almost any location on the planet, meaning you can explore the night markets in Bangkok, hover over mountainous regions like the Himalayas or zoom in on tiny islands and imagine you're sunbathing and smelling the sea.
sentences.chinese: 数字地图让你可以漫游地球上几乎任何地方，这意味着你可以探索曼谷的夜市，在喜马拉雅山脉等山区上空盘旋，或者聚焦于小岛，想象自己在享受日光浴、闻着海风的味道。

sentences.english: Of course, you won't experience the weather and culture in exactly the same way, but at least it's an option.
sentences.chinese: 当然，你无法以完全相同的方式体验天气和文化，但至少这是一个选择。

sentences.english: If you are a nature lover, it's possible to take an interactive virtual tour, with the option of virtual commentary, of a national park like Yellowstone in the USA.
sentences.chinese: 如果你是自然爱好者，可以参加美国黄石国家公园等地的互动式虚拟游览，并选择虚拟解说。

sentences.english: This area has a lot of volcanic activity, so you can watch geysers erupt, see sulphur lakes and virtually hike iconic trails.
sentences.chinese: 该地区火山活动频繁，因此你可以观看间歇泉喷发，观赏硫磺湖，并虚拟徒步标志性的小径。

sentences.english: Their website is full of videos walking you to famous viewpoints like Dragon's Mouth Spring and the cascading waterfall at Upper Falls.
sentences.chinese: 他们的网站上有很多视频，带你前往龙口泉和上瀑布的层叠瀑布等著名观景点。

sentences.english: And then there are oceanic adventures too.
sentences.chinese: 此外，还有海洋探险。

sentences.english: National Geographic offers virtual underwater experiences so you can dive with sharks and other marine life, see coral reefs come alive and explore sunken shipwrecks.
sentences.chinese: 《国家地理》提供虚拟水下体验，让你可以与鲨鱼和其他海洋生物一起潜水，观赏生机勃勃的珊瑚礁，探索沉没船只。

sentences.english: You can now tour many museums and landmarks virtually too, like The British Museum in London.
sentences.chinese: 现在，你还可以虚拟游览许多博物馆和地标建筑，例如伦敦的大英博物馆。

sentences.english: You can explore more than 60 galleries where you'll see priceless artefacts from around the world, like the Rosetta Stone, and famous paintings and sculptures.
sentences.chinese: 你可以探索60多个展厅，在那里你会看到来自世界各地的无价文物，如罗塞塔石碑，以及著名的绘画和雕塑。

sentences.english: The Taj Mahal is another place you can visit virtually and at a 360-degree angle, so you can scale heights that would be almost impossible if you were there in person.
sentences.chinese: 泰姬陵是另一个可以虚拟参观的地方，并且可以360度视角观看，因此你可以到达几乎不可能亲身到达的高度。

sentences.english: They say 'the world is your oyster'.
sentences.chinese: 人们常说"世界是你的牡蛎"。

sentences.english: So next time you get the travel bug, try a virtual escape.
sentences.chinese: 所以下次你燃起旅行欲望时，试试虚拟逃离吧。

sentences.english: A shoestring budget is no problem – you can still explore the world, and you don't even need a passport.
sentences.chinese: 预算有限也没问题——你仍然可以探索世界，甚至不需要护照。

title: When sandwiches are not so simple
titleChinese: 当三明治变得不再简单
paragraphs: For many of us, sandwiches are something simple. Something we can take to work or school to avoid having to cook lunch, something we can buy quickly and cheaply. For many of us, we don't even need to stop working to eat them. Sandwiches could possibly be the ultimate convenience food.

But now it seems people are realising that the humble sandwich can be so much more. There's nothing convenient about waiting an hour and paying five times the price of a supermarket sarnie, but that's exactly what customers at one London sandwich shop have been doing. What is it that makes people so keen to get their hands on these £12 sandwiches?

Firstly, it's the ingredients. As baking has become more popular, good quality bread is both available and expected. The brains behind many of these gourmet sandwich shops are often people who have worked in the kitchens of top, Michelin-starred restaurants. This means that they bring a fine-dining attitude to their sandwiches, sourcing the best and freshest ingredients, combining them in new and creative ways. Secondly, it's the size. Max Halley, owner of a similar sandwich shop, boasts that the sandwiches his shop makes are twice the size of most burgers.

Finally, having sandwiches that look both huge and delicious is perfect for social media. While they may be more expensive than supermarket sandwiches, they are far more accessible than many other dining options. Being enticing, affordable, and trendy is an almost guaranteed way to attract attention online and bring crowds to the shops' doors. That's what's leading some to spend most of their lunch hour queueing up for a bite.

And why not? They might be a bit too expensive to have every day, but taking time away from your desk to eat something that has been thoughtfully prepared from fresh, high-quality ingredients isn't a bad thing. It could be a good alternative to munching on industrially-produced supermarket sandwiches at your desk while staring at a spreadsheet.

vocabulary.entry: **ultimate** /ˈʌltɪmət/ adj. 终极的，极端的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The ultimate goal of the project is to reduce pollution.
vocabulary.translation: 这个项目的最终目标是减少污染。

vocabulary.entry: **convenience food** /kənˈviːniəns fuːd/ n. 方便食品，速食（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Convenience food is popular among busy people.
vocabulary.translation: 方便食品在忙碌的人群中很受欢迎。

vocabulary.entry: **humble** /ˈhʌmbl/ adj. 谦卑的，不起眼的
vocabulary.example: She comes from a humble background.

vocabulary.entry: **sarnie** /ˈsɑːni/ n. 三明治（英式口语）
vocabulary.example: I'll just grab a sarnie for lunch.

vocabulary.entry: **keen** /kiːn/ adj. 热衷的，渴望的
vocabulary.example: She was keen to get started on the project.
vocabulary.translation: 她渴望开始这个项目。

vocabulary.example: I'd love to get my hands on a copy of that book.

vocabulary.translation: 成分列表包括面粉、糖和鸡蛋。

vocabulary.entry: **gourmet** /ˈɡʊəmeɪ/ n. 美食家；adj. 美食的（书面语）

vocabulary.translation: 这家餐厅以高价提供美食。

vocabulary.example: The chef runs a Michelin-starred restaurant in Paris.
vocabulary.translation: 这位厨师在巴黎经营一家米其林星级餐厅。

vocabulary.entry: **fine-dining** /ˌfaɪn ˈdaɪnɪŋ/ n. 精致餐饮，高级餐厅用餐（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Fine-dining restaurants focus on high-quality ingredients and presentation.
vocabulary.translation: 精致餐饮餐厅注重高品质的食材和摆盘。

vocabulary.entry: **source** /sɔːs/ v. 获得（原材料）， sourcing（书面语）
vocabulary.example: We source our ingredients from local farmers.
vocabulary.translation: 我们从当地农民那里采购食材。

vocabulary.entry: **boast** /bəʊst/ v. 夸口，自夸（书面语）
vocabulary.example: He boasts that he can speak six languages.
vocabulary.translation: 他夸口说他会说六种语言。

vocabulary.entry: **burger** /ˈbɜːɡə(r)/ n. 汉堡包
vocabulary.example: I'll have a cheeseburger and fries.
vocabulary.translation: 我要一个芝士汉堡和薯条。

vocabulary.entry: **accessible** /əkˈsesəbl/ adj. 可获得的，易接近的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The website is accessible to all users.
vocabulary.translation: 所有用户都可以访问该网站。

vocabulary.entry: **dining option** /ˈdaɪnɪŋ ˌɒpʃn/ n. 用餐选择（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The city has many dining options for vegetarians.
vocabulary.translation: 这座城市为素食者提供了许多用餐选择。

vocabulary.entry: **enticing** /ɪnˈtaɪsɪŋ/ adj. 诱人的，有吸引力的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The shop window displayed an enticing array of cakes.
vocabulary.translation: 商店橱窗里陈列着一排诱人的蛋糕。

vocabulary.entry: **affordable** /əˈfɔːdəbl/ adj. 负担得起的，价格合理的
vocabulary.example: The hotel offers affordable accommodation for families.
vocabulary.translation: 这家酒店为家庭提供价格合理的住宿。

vocabulary.entry: **trendy** /ˈtrendi/ adj. 时髦的，流行的（口语）
vocabulary.example: This area has become very trendy among young people.
vocabulary.translation: 这个地区在年轻人中变得非常时髦。

vocabulary.entry: **queue up** /ˌkjuː ˈʌp/ phr. v. 排队等候（英式）
vocabulary.example: People queued up to buy tickets for the concert.
vocabulary.translation: 人们排队等候购买音乐会门票。

vocabulary.entry: **bite** /baɪt/ n. 一小口食物（口语）
vocabulary.example: I'm hungry – let's grab a bite to eat.
vocabulary.translation: 我饿了——我们吃点东西吧。

vocabulary.entry: **thoughtfully** /ˈθɔːtfəli/ adv. 深思熟虑地，精心地（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The meal was thoughtfully prepared by the chef.
vocabulary.translation: 这顿饭是厨师精心准备的。

vocabulary.entry: **alternative** /ɔːlˈtɜːnətɪv/ n. 可供选择的事物（书面语）
vocabulary.example: We have no alternative but to wait.
vocabulary.translation: 我们别无选择，只能等待。

vocabulary.entry: **munch** /mʌntʃ/ v. 大声咀嚼，用力嚼（口语）
vocabulary.example: He was munching on an apple.
vocabulary.translation: 他正在大声嚼着一个苹果。

vocabulary.entry: **industrially-produced** /ɪnˈdʌstriəli prəˈdjuːst/ adj. 工业化生产的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Industrially-produced food often contains additives.
vocabulary.translation: 工业化生产的食品通常含有添加剂。

vocabulary.entry: **spreadsheet** /ˈspredʃiːt/ n. 电子表格
vocabulary.example: She spends hours each day working on spreadsheets.
vocabulary.translation: 她每天花数小时处理电子表格。

sentences.chinese: 对我们许多人来说，我们甚至不需要停下工作来吃它们。

sentences.english: Sandwiches could possibly be the ultimate convenience food.
sentences.chinese: 三明治可能是终极的方便食品。

sentences.english: There's nothing convenient about waiting an hour and paying five times the price of a supermarket sarnie, but that's exactly what customers at one London sandwich shop have been doing.

sentences.chinese: 随着烘焙变得越来越流行，人们期待买到优质面包。

sentences.chinese: 虽然它们可能比超市三明治更贵，但比许多其他餐饮选择要容易获得得多。

sentences.chinese: 诱人、价格合理且时尚，几乎是吸引网络关注、让人们涌向店门的保证。
